col.availability-tooltip: Percentage of the time the vehicle was connected and available for charging/discharging during this period.

totals.savings-tooltip:
This is your savings compared to standard charging.

Standard charging: every time you plugged in, charge immediately to your configured maximum battery percentage — without a smart schedule.

The cost of standard charging is calculated based on your charging history in two variants:
 • Fixed: standard charging kWh × monthly average contract prices (CBS).
 • Dynamic: standard charging kWh × the same dynamic energy prices.

data-table.estimated-tooltip: Historical data was not always complete. Missing values have been interpolated where possible. There may still be gaps in the data. The charging status was not historically logged and is therefore unknown.

reset-dialog.reimport-explanation: Re-runs the historical data import from FlexMeasures. Existing data is kept; missing data is added. Use this when the initial import was incomplete or after a software update.
reset-dialog.full-explanation: Deletes all charging history and statistics, then re-imports from FlexMeasures. Use this when the database is corrupted or after a schema change.
reset-dialog.duration-note: Importing historical charging data from FlexMeasures takes up to **5 minutes per month** of history.
reset-dialog.full-warning: This will permanently delete all local charging data. This cannot be undone.
reset-dialog.success: Done. Historical data is being re-imported — the Data page will gradually fill up.

intro.p1: By monitoring your grid connection, V2G Liberty learns your household energy patterns. That leads to better predictions and smarter schedules.
intro.p2: For Dutch users: a valuable preparation for the end of net metering. Once it ends, this configuration will be required.
intro.req-smart-meter-desc: Reports power per phase in real time.
intro.req-cable-desc: A USB P1 port cable or similar (~€15).
intro.req-integration-desc: E.g. the DSMR Smart Meter integration, exposing the meter as sensor entities.

meter.intro: The cumulative meter readings are what your energy bill is settled on, per tariff. There are always two tariffs — with a single tariff, tariff 2 simply stays at the same value. These were recognised automatically — please check them before continuing.
meter.import-sub: total energy taken from the grid
meter.export-sub: total energy fed back to the grid

choose-sensor.title: Choose sensor
choose-sensor.search-info: Prefilled with what you are setting up — every word has to match. Clear or edit it if your integration names things differently.
choose-sensor.select-first: Choose a sensor from the list first — search above if you don't see it.
choose-sensor.unsuitable-title: This sensor does not fit here
choose-sensor.unsuitable-body: This sensor measures %{unit}, not what this field needs. V2G Liberty cannot use it here and the schedules would be wrong. Pick another sensor, or press OK again to use it anyway.
choose-sensor.help-summary: Help — which sensor do I pick?
choose-sensor.help-power-1: Pick the power on one phase, in W or kW, measured at your meter — a value that changes all the time. Consumption is what you take from the grid, production what you feed back. Phase numbering follows your meter, so pick the sensor whose phase matches the row you are filling in.
choose-sensor.help-power-2: A sensor for a single appliance (a heat pump, a charger) measures only that device, not the whole connection.
choose-sensor.help-meter-1: Pick a total in kWh that only ever goes up — the same kind of number your meter shows. Import is what you took from the grid; export is what you fed back. With DSMR these are usually named energy consumption / production tariff 1 / 2.
choose-sensor.help-meter-2: Not sure between two? Compare the value with the display on your meter — the numbers should match.

enabled.title: V2G Liberty load balancer module enabled
enabled.info:
The V2G Liberty load balancer module is currently enabled.

**Important**
This module is provided without any guarantees. Use it at your own risk.

Please consult a certified electrician what maximum power can be set on the charger.

**Configuration**

- The Charger hostname must be set to `127.0.0.1`

- The port number must be set to `5020`

For further details please consult `readme.md` in the folder `load_balancer`.

not_enabled.title: V2G Liberty load balancer module not enabled
not_enabled.info:
A load balancer is recommended (but it is not mandatory). It enables the charger to have a higher maximum charge amperage setting while maintaining safe power levels. This leads to more efficient charging and increased yields.

_Unfortunately the Wallbox Quasar 1 load balancer does not work correctly with V2G Liberty, please consult `readme.md` in the folder `load_balancer` for a workaround._

Please consult a certified electrician what maximum power can be set on the charger.

Open the app, go to Settings (⚙-icon in the top right) -> Network -> Ethernet (or WiFi) ->  IP-address. Then you are asked to connect to the charger via Bluetooth.

car-battery-usable-capacity.description:
This is the the maximum energy storage capacity of the car's battery that can be used for driving/charging/discharging. This often is lower than the advertised capacity.

Find a reliable value on [Electric Vehicle Database](https://ev-database.org).

**Battery health**
If a battery get’s older it usually degrades and cannot contain as much energy as when it was new. It’s advised to take this into account here. Do this by looking for the State of Health (SoH) in the cars the menu’s.
*E.g: The SoH is 11/12 and the original usable capacity was 59kWh, then use a value of 54kWh.*

roundtrip-efficiency.description:
This is the efficiency of a cycle of charge and discharge and includes charger and car. A typical value is 85%.
A higher setting will result in more cycling in the schedule, a lower value will result in the schedule being idle more often.

car-energy-consumption.description:
The average electricity usage of your car in Watt-hour (Wh) per kilometer.

In most cars you can find historical data in the menu's or see [Electric Vehicle Database](https://ev-database.org).

Normally this is between 140 (very efficient) and 300 (rather in-efficient vans).

Make sure you use the right 'unit of measure': Wh/km.

allowed-duration-above-max.description:
When the car connects with a SoC higher than the upper limit, how long may the schedule take to bring the SoC back to this maximum?

A longer duration gives opportunity for a more optimal schedule but might have a (minor) degradation effect on the battery.
This duration is excluding the (minimum) time it takes to get back to the desired maximum under normal cycling conditions.

car-battery-lower-charge-limit.header: Lower charge limit for car battery
car-battery-lower-charge-limit.description:
The automated schedule will never discharge below this value.
**Effects on automated charging**
If the car returns with and SoC below this value, the battery will directly be charged to this limit, before automated (scheduled) charging.

**Effects on earnings**
A high value results in always having a greater driving range available, even when not planned, but less capacity available for dis-charge and so lesser earnings.
A lower value results in sometimes a smaller driving range available for un-planned drives but there is always more capacity for discharge and so more earnings.

**Battery life**
Some research suggests battery life is shorter if the SoC is below 15% for a longer period.

**Odd car behaviour**
In some cars the SoC every now and then skips a number, eg. from 21 to 19%, skipping 20%. This might result in toggling charging behaviour around this minimum SoC. If this happens try a value one higher or lower.

car-battery-upper-charge-limit.header: Upper charge limit for car battery
car-battery-upper-charge-limit.description:
The schedule will use this limit for regular automated /scheduled charging.
**Effects on earnings**
A low setting reduces schedule flexibility and so the capability to earn money and reduce emissions.

When a calendar item is present with a charge target above this limit, the schedule will ignore this limit and try to charge the battery to the target at the start of the calendar.

**Battery life**
Some research suggests battery life is shorter if the SoC is above 85% for a longer period (days).

optimisation-mode.description:
**Price optimisation**
This will maximise revenues / savings based on dynamic tarifs.

**Emission minimisation**
This minimises CO₂ emissions due to electricity production.

If you choose either the other will benefit in general.

electricity-contract.alert: Please configure an electricity contract, V2G Liberty needs this to work.
electricity-contract.selection-header: What electricity contract do you have?
electricity-contract.amber-description:
For the electricity contract **Amber Electric (Australia)** V2G Liberty gets electricity prices via the [Amber Electric Home Assistant integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/amberelectric). Please make sure this is installed and functioning.

Please enter the entity_id of the consumption (`sensor.****_general_forecast`) and production (`sensor.****_feed_in_forecast`) entities that are populated by the Amber Electric integration.
electricity-contract.octopus-description:
For the electricity contract **Octopus Energy (Great Britain)** V2G Liberty gets electricity prices via the Octopus API.

Please enter the import / export code that is specific for your contract. E.g. `AGILE-FLEX-22-11-25` / `AGILE-OUTGOING-19-05-13`. If you do not have them, the Octopus help-desk can supply them.
electricity-contract.nl-sub-header: For the electricity contract **%{contract} (%{country})** you get an all included price from our backend.
electricity-contract.nl-generic-description:
While not needed, you can add extra price components.

VAT and markup are used for transforming the raw price data (from the cloud) to net price to be shown in UI:
(market-price-per-kwh + markup-per-kwh) * (100 + VAT)/100

If both are 0 the price from the cloud remains unchanged.
